subject: Hotpath vs Coldstore observability SKU structuring — AtlasHealth commercial options
messages:
From: Piper Thompson <piper@atlashealth.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@atlashealth.io>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Structuring observability SKUs for hotpath vs coldstore

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team found the tracing latency visualizer and real-time session view very compelling. Were now trying to map those capabilities to a commercial model that fits our reporting/finance constraints. High level:

- We have two logical workloads: a hotpath (real-time error traces + 30d indexed retention; used by product & oncall) and a coldstore (90-365d archive for audits and analytics).
- Hotpath: ~150k trace events/day today, expected +40% next 6 months. Very sensitive to p95 latency and SLO.
- Coldstore: ~4TB/quarter, queries mostly ad-hoc (daily/weekly).
- Also interested in advanced dashboards for executive reporting (3-5 dashboards, ~6 users) and trace sampling/ingestion controls.

Can you share: 1) a clear SKU split for hotpath vs coldstore (how we should think about retention tiers, ingestion credits, index vs archive pricing), 2) pilot credit options for a 3-month validation, and 3) suggested concession/discount structure for an annual commit (~$250k ARR target).

I attached a workbook that maps our expected volumes — happy to walk through with Ben or someone from pricing. Looking to get a commercial proposal that separates the real-time SLA-sensitive piece from long-term archival so our finance team can sign off.

Thanks,
Piper
Piper Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering, AtlasHealth
P: 415-555-0123

Attachment: AtlasHealth_OBSV_SKU_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Piper Thompson <piper@atlashealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Structuring observability SKUs for hotpath vs coldstore

Hi Piper,

Really appreciate the detail in the workbook — that made this much easier to model. Quick summary of what Id propose below, then Ben will follow with a line-item export and workbook breakdown. Lauren and I will handle pilot terms and the contract flow.

Summary proposal (high level):

1) SKU split: Hotpath (real-time retention + tracing) vs Coldstore (archival/long-term queries)
   - Hotpath SKU: priced on ingestion rate (ingest credits) + per-concurrent-traces SLA surcharge. Includes 30d indexed retention and priority compute for p95 SLO.
   - Coldstore SKU: priced on GB-month of retained storage + query egress (ad-hoc queries priced per TB scanned). Default 90d tier, optional 180/365 upgrade.

2) Advanced Dashboards: seatless dashboard SKU (per-dashboard or per-50k monthly view pool) OR seat-based for heavy interactive users. For Atlass profile (3-5 dashboards, ~6 heavy users) we recommend seat-based at a discounted seat rate with dashboard render credits included.

3) Pilot credits & term: 3-month pilot with: $15k ingestion credits (hotpath), 2TB coldstore credits, and waived dashboard fees for the pilot. If you convert to a 12-month annual commit, we apply the pilot credit against first invoice.

4) Commercial concessions (examples we typically consider):
   - 12-month commit: 10-18% off list on add-on SKUs depending on commit size (we can tier to 12% for $250k ARR).
   - Multi-year: addtl 5% on year-two+ or guaranteed price protection.
   - Volume bands: if hotpath ingest grows above 300k traces/day we trigger a reprice review and guaranteed marginal dilution band.

Next steps: Ben, can you drop the workbook with a line-itemized price table (hotpath ingest bands, coldstore GB-month, dashboard seat vs render credits) and an example amortization schedule that shows first-year and run-rate savings? Lauren, Ill include you on the SOW/pilot terms doc that we can deliver by Thursday.

Piper — happy to do a 30-minute commercial call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best,
Grace O
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Pricing workbook & line items for AtlasHealth (hotpath/coldstore)

Hi team,

Attached is the exported workbook and a PDF summary (redwood-pricing-summary.pdf). Key line items included in the sheet:

- Hotpath ingest bands (ingest credits): 0-100k, 100k-300k, 300k+. Example price per 1000 traces and suggested discounts at commit bands.
- Hotpath SLA surcharge: applied as percentage of hotpath bill for priority compute (p95-focused routing).
- Coldstore storage: $/GB-month with tiered discounts at 50TB, 200TB bands; query egress priced per TB scanned with a free baseline for lightweight analytics.
- Dashboard options: seat-based rate ($/seat/month) vs render-pool (per 50k renders/month).
- Pilot package: credit lines and a proposed SOW (pilot-terms-draft.docx) with success criteria (ingest rate, dashboard performance, export latency).

I also added two commercial scenarios for $250k ARR:
- Scenario A (balanced): split 60/40 hotpath/coldstore -> 12% discount on add-ons, pilot credit applied to month-1 invoice.
- Scenario B (hotpath-heavy): anticipated growth to 300k/day; we propose an initial 10% commit discount + a growth-triggered dilution schedule (reprice at 300k/day to ensure margin neutrality).

File list: AtlasHealth_OBSV_SKU_workbook.xlsx (detailed bands), redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (one-pager), pilot-terms-draft.docx (SOW).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (PDF), pilot-terms-draft.docx (docx)

Grace / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and for laying out two concrete scenarios. Marco here (finance) — a couple quick clarifying q's before we schedule the exec-level commercial review: 

1) How are pilot credits amortized if we convert mid-quarter? Do they apply against usage first or against upfront invoice?
2) For the hotpath SLA surcharge, can you provide an absolute example invoice for month-1 at our current volumes so we can model cashflow?
3) On dashboards: our preference is seat-based but we need a firm # for the first year to bake into our budget (well likely start with 6 seats). Can you include a 1-year seat commitment example and the delta to switch to seatless render pool if we exceed view volumes?

If you can drop those three line examples into the workbook (or a short note), well lock a 45-minute call for Thursday afternoon to get sign-off from procurement.

Appreciate it — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Marco Ruiz
Director, Finance — AtlasHealth
